posts.body_html:
Technically speaking, this clone is called S. leucophylla clone A Escambia Co, FL, but given that it's a proven giant, I think it should be call as such.

This clone comes from my good homie and flytrap legend Matt Miller of www.flytrapcare.com So here's the story: Eric Morrow, another homie from back in the day who was once very active on this forum, had a huge collection of mostly seed grown Sarracenia. Regretfully, he got out of the hobby a few years ago for personal reasons and Matt was able to acquire his entire collection (thank Jesus!). I remember Matt told me one winter he spent an enormous amount of time and energy (with some help) repotting/dividing Eric's entire collection. The plants were then babied and well cared for as though Jesus was watching from afar...you don't want to slack and feel the wrath of the lord for not doing a good job at the Lord's work (aka growing crops for Jesus). Anyways, fast forward to maybe two years ago, Matt and I were chatting and he brought up this freakin giant leuco that produced some absolutely jaw droppingly enormous traps. I saw the first few pics below.....My eyes instantly bulged out with envy and somehow he ended up sending me a division, YESSSSSSSSSSSS!!!!!!


So here are the pics that Matt took and sent me, these traps are GIANT maaan!


Lord, kindly have mercy:





So those pictures were from last year. Here are Matt's photos of the same clone this year, it's performing consistently, which is a great sign of quality genetics. Matt mentioned it's consistently one of the best specimens in his collection over the past 4 years!











Matt asked me how it has done for me and while my plant is still small, I can say it has a really nice look to it outdoors! It's also quite vigorous and despite the traps not being fully mature in size, they're already really showy, it's hard to walk by and not notice it. My pics turned out blurry so I have to take new ones, to be continued.....

posts.body_html: There has to be some genes floating around the leucos in Escambia County, Florida.  This is the third "GIANT" leuco clone I know of from there, and they're all slightly different in coloration, especially the lip, so I think they're all different clones.  Mike Wang, Matt Miller, and Jeremiah Harris each have one.
